summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on MWF hemodialysis via a left femoral tunneled catheter, HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin was admitted after outpatient blood cultures from her femoral dialysis catheter grew gram-positive cocci, with purulent drainage and pain at the catheter site. Cultures confirmed MRSA bacteremia; she was treated with vancomycin dosed per hemodialysis protocol and Infectious Disease was consulted. Transthoracic echocardiogram showed no evidence of endocarditis. Given concern for catheter source, the left femoral tunneled catheter was removed and temporary access was maintained during a line holiday while surveillance blood cultures cleared; a new right femoral tunneled hemodialysis catheter was subsequently placed. Due to long-standing inferior vena cava stenosis/occlusion contributing to access difficulty and hypotension, she underwent venoplasty and IVC stent placement. During the dialysis holiday she developed severe hyperkalemia with bradycardia and epigastric pain, which resolved after dialysis through the new catheter. Warfarin was held around procedures and then restarted and titrated with plans for outpatient INR monitoring. She had relative hypotension managed with fluids and increased midodrine, transient eosinophilia that normalized by discharge, and constipation treated with bowel regimen. She was discharged to an extended care facility with plans to complete a 6-week course of vancomycin with dialysis, continue ESRD and HIV medications, and follow up on pending blood cultures and anticoagulation monitoring.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease with very low CD4 count
Compression of vein / inferior vena cava stenosis requiring stent
Atrial fibrillation on long-term anticoagulation (warfarin) with abnormal coagulation profile during admission
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications (history)
